geometry_edits.rationale: Align the access carve to the verified program-side threshold.
Make the entry subtraction more legible from the street edge.
Increase the vertical depth of the carve so it reads as a true public seam.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the public threshold aligned to the verified access side and strengthen the frontage response without disturbing the dominant mass.
Widen the access carve slightly so the ground void reads more clearly as a usable public entry condition.
Extend the notch vertically enough to sharpen the sectioned threshold and improve the public void's legibility.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early-stage mass with one dominant bent slab-like gesture and a single major notch/void that reads in all four views. The silhouette is not arbitrary: it maintains a continuous low-rise bar condition while introducing a clear spatial cut, so it avoids pure boxiness and supports the neighborhood-living brief. The blue access edge is met with a legible ground response only partially, though the notch/void gives a public threshold signal rather than a sealed frontage. The form resonates with the references through courtyard/void-centered low-rise composition and some terrace/bridge logic, but it is less distributed and less porous than the stronger precedents. Program fit is acceptable because the mass can plausibly host mixed neighborhood uses with active ground and calmer upper volume, but the section is still somewhat generic and would benefit from a clearer access-facing carve or courtyard articulation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and ceremonially expressive than this neighborhood-living brief; do not copy the scalloped roof language directly.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise pavilion logic with a carved central opening and a bridge-like upper link that keeps the mass readable from multiple views.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger campus-like assembly; candidate should only borrow the courtyard/terrace relation, not the scale or multiplicity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard-centered multi-part composition with terraced low-rise blocks that preserve a clear public interior.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more open and transparent than the candidate; the candidate’s ground response is still comparatively sealed.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated horizontal massing with a voided core and a folded/site-responsive roof line.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Topographically conditioned and more distributed than the candidate; keep the terraced gesture but avoid over-fragmentation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, winged composition around a shared open space, with circulation and section doing real spatial work.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More explicitly multi-wing and layered; candidate is still closer to a single mass with a cut than a full interlock.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes around a courtyard with upper-level bridging and setbacks that preserve a legible public void.

warnings: Parcel containment was not deterministically verifiable from the provided views, so no hard-gate containment claim is made here.
The form is coherent, but the access-edge response remains the weakest program relation.
Sectional support for neighborhood living is present only at a basic level; it does not yet strongly differentiate ground/public from upper/private masses.
